evidence: Cic. Off. 1.16: potest et vidēre et explicāre ratiōnem
terms.comment: With an object or an indirect question (Explicā, quaesō, quid in capite quārtō sit, Traupman 26); for “explained that …” use docēre or expōnere with an accusative and infinitive. Cicero’s perfect is explicāvī; explicuī comes in with Vergil and Livy (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: set out, explain (also with an accusative and infinitive)
evidence: Cic. Rep. 1.22: coepit ratiōnem hujus operis scientissimē Gallus expōnere (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: explain that, show (with an accusative and infinitive)
evidence: Cic. Att. 16.8.1: docuī per litterās, id nec opus esse nec fierī posse
Cic. Off. 1.94: facilius intellegī quam explānārī potest

phrases.latin: sī nēmō ex mē quaerat, sciō; sī quaerentī explicāre velim, nesciō
phrases.english: if nobody asks me, I know; if I want to explain it to someone who asks, I don’t

phrases.latin: Inter edendum pater quid eō diē vīsūrī essent explicāvit
phrases.english: Over breakfast Dad explained what they were going to see that day
phrases.source: Libellus II, Sintra: castellum et puteus

phrases.latin: Tum pater docuit nōmen illud, ā rēge Francōrum antīquō ductum, 'pugnā clārum' significāre.
phrases.english: Then Dad explained that the name, which comes from an old king of the Franks, means “famous in battle”.
phrases.source: Libellus V, Lisbōna: castellum et ōceanārium
